category.name: Electricity & Circuits
category.description: Electric charge, current, potential difference, resistance, and electrical energy.

lessons.name: Ohm's Law
lessons.description: Current flowing through an ohmic conductor is directly proportional to voltage and inversely proportional to resistance.

variables.name: Voltage / Potential Difference
variables.description: Electric potential difference across component (SI unit: Volt V)

variables.name: Electric Current
variables.description: Flow rate of electric charge (SI unit: Ampere A = C/s)

variables.name: Electrical Resistance
variables.description: Opposition to charge flow (SI unit: Ohm Ω = V/A)

worked_example.problem: A 12 V battery is connected to a resistor of 4 Ω. Calculate the current flowing in the circuit.

validation.error_message: Resistance must be greater than zero.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Ohm's law forms the foundation of circuit analysis for linear resistive components.

lessons.name: Electrical Power
lessons.description: Rate at which electrical energy is converted into heat, light, or mechanical work in a circuit.

variables.name: Electrical Power
variables.description: Dissipated electrical power (SI unit: Watt W)

worked_example.problem: An electric heater draws 5 A of current when plugged into a 220 V outlet. Find its power rating.

sections.title: Joule Heating
sections.content: Using Ohm's law, electrical power can also be expressed as P = I²R or P = V²/R.
